The bug where escape characters were stripped before non-meta characters during CSV parsing has been identified and fixed.

### Cause of the Bug
In [`Lexer.readEscape`](file:///Users/nothing/prometheus_workdir_microstudy/csv_3_group_c_fix/src/main/java/org/apache/commons/csv/Lexer.java#L87-L114), unhandled characters in the `switch` statement were returned directly via `return c;` in the default case, rather than returning `Constants.END_OF_STREAM` when the character was not a meta-character (delimiter, escape, quote character, or comment start). Because [`CSVLexer`](file:///Users/nothing/prometheus_workdir_microstudy/csv_3_group_c_fix/src/main/java/org/apache/commons/csv/CSVLexer.java#L164) only appends both the escape character and the subsequent character when `readEscape()` returns `Constants.END_OF_STREAM`, non-meta characters had their preceding escape character dropped.

### Solution
Updated [`Lexer.readEscape()`](file:///Users/nothing/prometheus_workdir_microstudy/csv_3_group_c_fix/src/main/java/org/apache/commons/csv/Lexer.java#L108-L115) so that characters not matching predefined escape sequences (`\n`, `\r`, `\t`, `\b`, `\f`) are checked:
- If the character is a meta-character (`isDelimiter(c) || isEscape(c) || isQuoteChar(c) || isCommentStart(c)`), return `c`.
- Otherwise, return `Constants.END_OF_STREAM`.

The focused patch has been generated and saved to `negative_fix.patch`. All tests in `CucumberTest` pass.
